text:
B: Hi! Sorry, I think I was on mute. Can you hear me?
A: Yes, I can hear you now. Hi. I'm Joanne.
B: Sana. Hi. Erm, sorry, I'm a bit nervous, I don't really do video calls.
A: Oh gosh, me neither. I think everyone's nervous. Erm, where are you?
B: Luton. You?
A: Basingstoke. Hampshire.
B: Oh, I've never been. Is that your dog? I can see a little bit of fur at the bottom.
A: Yes, sorry, that's Biscuit. He's asleep. He's a cockapoo, he's quite old. He's had a dodgy tummy this week, so he's been on chicken and rice like a little invalid.
B: Aw, bless him. My son would go mad for him. He wants a dog so bad, but we're in a flat, so... maybe one day. Right now it's dinosaurs.
A: How old is he?
B: Five. Zayan. He's in Year One. He's obsessed with Bluey and dinosaurs. He knows all the long names, like, I can't even say them and he's correcting me. Erm, sorry, I'm talking about him a lot.
A: No, that's lovely. Do you work as well?
B: Yeah, I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. So prepping veg and serving and washing up. It's term-time only, which is good with Zayan.
A: That sounds quite full on, actually. All those children.
B: It is, but I kind of like it. You get to know the kids. I always remember which ones have allergies, the cook says I'm better than the list. Erm, what do you do?
A: I'm a planner, at the council. So people's extensions, and that sort of thing. Mostly I sit at home reading drawings with the radio on.
B: Oh, that sounds really clever. Like, a proper job.
A: Oh, gosh, it's not, really. I sort of drifted into it. And there's a bit where you have to speak at a committee, and I absolutely dread that. I'm not sure that's very helpful, sorry.
B: No, I'd be the same. I'd hate speaking in front of people.
A: Do you want to stay at the school, do you think?
B: Erm, I'd kind of like to be a teaching assistant. I see them every day and I think I could do it. There's a Level 3 course, but I'm scared about going back to studying. I didn't finish college before, cos I had Zayan, so... I don't know if that makes sense.
A: It does. But honestly, it sounds like you'd be really good at it. You clearly know the children.
B: Thank you. That's nice of you.
A: My sister went back to studying in her thirties. She was terrified and she loved it in the end.
B: Really? Okay. That makes me feel a bit better.
A: Erm, sorry, I've lost track of time. Are we nearly done?
B: I think so, yeah. It was really nice to meet you. Give Biscuit a stroke for me.
A: I will. Good luck with the course, Sana.
